proposal.name: Rebuild closed modeled drafts on retry

issue_plan.name: Rebuild closed modeled drafts on retry
issue_plan.summary: A writer's retry after a person closes a failed modeled draft will build the same ratified statements again in a new pull request. Two modeled amendments first authorize that transition and its recovery across crashes; one plumbing change then connects them to the factory, its posts, dashboard cards and /act. The issues preserve retries that watch an open modeled draft, explain how to rebuild or revise at each stage, and update the decision record and documentation.

issues.title: Authorize retrying a closed modeled draft in the issue protocol
issues.body:
Project: factory/protocol

The owner chose option 1 of #945 on 19 November 2026: after a person closes a modeled build's failed draft without merging it, a writer's retry builds the same ratified statements again, from their ratification, in a new pull request. This covers a draft left by failure of the factory's own gate and that draft after an earlier retry watched it and CI's gate failed. Closing the pull request alone must not start a build.

Amend the existing issue protocol to authorize this path. Today OthersClose clears the failure and enters closed, Retry requires failed, and Rebuild requires the factory's own gate failure. Represent enough provenance to retain the eligible failed draft and its ratified proposal across watch, CI failure and closure. Distinguish this case from a merged pull request or an unrelated closed pull request; merely being closed must not confer rebuild authority. A retry after the human close must work whether the watcher has already reported that close or discovers it while handling the command.

The authorized transition returns to ratified with the same proposal and ratification. Clear the earlier pull request's head, CI result, lock, scope and merge state, and reset the stopped-build count as an explicit retry does. Only a human with repository write access can request it. A retry must stay attached to its eligible build rather than authorize a later attempt. While a modeled draft remains open, retry still watches that pull request. Preserve the existing plan-draft Rebuild path, stopped-build retries, revision and new-ratification path, and all current-head, scope, lock and trusted-base merge requirements.

Explicitly amend the pinned RebuildsOwnFailures guarantee and the RebuildAfterCI known bug to admit this closed-draft case while continuing to reject rebuilding an open pull request merely because CI failed. Keep BuildStartsClean meaningful. Update IssueProtocol.tla, the Go core and contracts, explorer and project README together. Include witnesses for own-gate failure then close then retry, and own-gate failure then watch then CI failure then close then retry, followed by a successful build, another failed draft or a stopped build. Include counterexamples for unauthorized retry, rebuilding without an eligible close, replacing merged work and retaining the old pull request's evidence. Preserve the existing follow-up protocol and ordinary watcher API until the integration issue connects the new path.

This is a modeled amendment under D-0064 and D-0105, refining D-0202/D-0209 and the retry boundary in D-0191/D-0218. Inspect their dependents before drafting it. Obtain the owner's ratification of the changed statements through the normal amendment flow before changing pinned statements or ratified.lock; ratifying this issue plan alone does not ratify those statements. Run the complete factory/protocol verification gate, including model checks, witnesses, known bugs, Go proof and conformance. At merge, record the amendment with the decisions CLI and keep SPEC.md, README.md and docs/factory.md accurate under AGENTS.md, using a merger follow-up where factory scope requires it, before the next issue starts. Describe the amended core without claiming the watcher already uses the new path.

issues.title: Recover a rebuild requested after a person closes a modeled draft
issues.body:
Project: factory/recovery

After the protocol amendment for #945 merges, amend the recovery core for the same authorized retry: a human writer asks to build the existing ratified statements again after a person closes a failed modeled draft without merging it, including a draft previously watched by a retry and subsequently failed by CI. The existing recovery model cannot take this path: GiveRetry excludes closed pull requests and previously watched drafts, and a predecessor closed before replacement intent is recorded produces an answer without a build.

Represent this new retry authority explicitly, with enough failed-draft and closure provenance to distinguish it from ordinary closure. Record which retry starts the new attempt and which closed draft it replaces in state every watcher can recover before answering the retry and starting its build. A human close stays a human close; the factory must neither close that pull request again nor pretend it retired it. The new attempt owns its run, code publication, pull request and answer, and preserves the ratification. It may succeed, stop partway or leave another failed draft, which can in turn be closed and retried. An earlier watch of the closed draft must neither block the new attempt nor supply watch or gate authority for its successor.

Preserve one answer per command and build, one run and at most one pull request per build, and at most one open pull request for the work. Only the lease holder takes effects. A superseded run can be recorded only as its own result and cannot publish for the successor. A merged predecessor cannot be replaced. Keep the existing plan-draft replacement rules, including recording intent before the factory closes an open draft and answering without a build when someone closed that plan draft before the record. A watched modeled draft remains unreplaceable while open; the new authority requires the person's close and subsequent retry. Keep stopped-build retries and existing watch/readiness/merge behavior.

Update WatcherRecovery.tla, the proved Go core and contracts, explorer and project README. Explicitly qualify the existing rule that a watched draft is never replaced and the closed-before-intent outcome, rather than silently weakening their statements. Under the existing fairness assumptions, eligible retries and their builds must eventually be answered across crashes and a second watcher. Add witnesses for rebuilding an already closed failed draft, rebuilding after an earlier watch, recovering each interrupted replacement stage, repeated failed attempts and a stopped replacement. Add known bugs for duplicate answers or runs, reusing the predecessor's gate or result, replacing merged work, bypassing the required retry/record and opening a successor while the predecessor is still open. Preserve the exported operations and defaults the current watcher uses until the integration issue.

Basis: #945's selected behavior, the preceding protocol amendment, D-0069/D-0074, D-0203/D-0210, D-0218 and D-0225. Inspect dependents and have the owner ratify the statement changes through the normal amendment flow before updating pinned statements or ratified.lock. Run the complete factory/recovery gate, including safety and liveness checks, witnesses, known bugs, Go proof and conformance. At merge, record the amendment with the decisions CLI and keep SPEC.md, README.md and docs/factory.md accurate, with any scope-required merger follow-up completed before integration. The documentation must distinguish core support from the watcher behavior still awaiting integration.

issues.title: Build closed modeled drafts again and offer the same action everywhere
issues.body:
Kind: plumbing

Connect the two ratified #945 core amendments to internal/factory and internal/dashboard. The owner chose that a writer's retry after a person closes a failed modeled draft builds the same ratified statements again from their ratification, on a new branch and in a new pull request, without another proposal or ratification. This must work both directly after the factory's own gate failure and after a retry watched that draft and CI's gate failed. While the modeled draft is open, retry continues to watch it.

Update thread/marker interpretation, command dispatch, closure handling, rebuild logic and both core adapters so an eligible human close remains retryable. Preserve the failed build's identity and ratification through subsequent watch, CI-failure and closed posts. Recognize existing eligible histories from their durable posts, including histories written before this change; do not infer eligibility from an arbitrary closed marker or silently substitute an older proposal when evidence cannot be read. Handle a retry posted after the person closed the draft but before the watcher reported the close, as well as one posted after that report. Closure alone starts nothing, and stale or queued retries cannot rebuild a later attempt. Route the transition and effects through the amended cores.

Find and validate the commit containing the same modeled ratification, including the retained source commit on later attempts. Extend the modeled runBuild/worktree path, which currently starts only from origin/<branch>, to create the retry's branch from that commit rather than from the failed draft's code. Keep project/branch validation and both inline and saved-proposal handling. Give each retry a durable replacement record, its own build/run identity and its own pull request; leave the human-closed draft and its work available to read. Run the normal modeled synthesis, verification and review, and apply the existing publication and trusted-base merge rules to the successor. A new failure may leave another draft, and a stopped replacement retains enough information for the next retry. If the ratification cannot be recovered, answer once with an actionable explanation and the revise/new-ratification route, expose that limitation on its card, and avoid an endless build or poll failure.

Make the factory's failed-build post, CI-failure post, closed post, retry answer and refused-revision guidance describe the actual actions: retry watches an open modeled draft; closing an eligible failed draft and then retrying rebuilds the same statements; revising changes the proposal and requires ratification. An ineligible retry must explain the available next step rather than only say nothing failed. Keep commands and their meanings in the unclipped closing of long posts. Update the dashboard's server-derived Takes and retry copy, public and /act cards, confirmation, posted feedback and history to match. An eligible closed draft offers rebuilding and revision; unavailable ratification offers revision. /act must accept only the commands its current card permits and send the existing retry command. History must attribute the earlier close to the person, not claim the factory closed it.

Acceptance tests must exercise the real factory poll/build/publication paths with controlled builders and GitHub/repository fixtures for both failure histories and both close-report timings. Assert the unchanged ratified hash/lock, exact starting commit, distinct branch/run/pull request, fresh checks and review, one command answer, and no reopening, readying or merging of the old draft. Cover a second failed draft closed and retried, a stopped replacement, an older eligible history, a missing ratification on a fresh clone, merged or ineligible predecessors, unauthorized commands and a retry queued before a later failure. Interrupt each new durable effect and resume with another watcher to demonstrate no duplicated run, post or pull request and no stale publication. Retain regressions for open modeled drafts watching again, plan-draft replacement including its close-before-record rule, ordinary CI retries, issue closure and trusted-base handling. Test served dashboard state, rendered action/guidance, /act acceptance/refusal and posted feedback for the same scenarios, including clipped posts. Update existing pinned acceptance expectations only for the explicitly changed closed-modeled-draft behavior and its guidance.

Keep SPEC.md, README.md and docs/factory.md current in this change, within the README's 400-line limit. Record #945's selected behavior and the amended boundaries using the decisions CLI and the repository's ratified-plan rules; complete any decision-writing merger follow-up before moving on. Basis: the two preceding amendments, D-0156, D-0191, D-0218, D-0225 and D-0237/D-0238. Run the affected factory and dashboard tests and the required checks in AGENTS.md. This work overlaps #933 in internal/factory: whichever merges second must incorporate the first and check their combined behavior against the resulting base.
